Start here (15 minutes)

You don't need more leads before you've followed up on the ones you already have. A good share of the calls a home-service business gets go unanswered, usually because you're on a roof, in a crawlspace, under a sink or with a customer. Industry call-tracking studies put it somewhere between 1 in 7 and 1 in 4. And most homeowners who get a quote and don't hear back simply hire whoever followed up first.

This kit fixes two leaks:

  1. Missed calls. Someone called, nobody picked up, and they're dialing your competitor.
  2. Quiet quotes. You sent a price, they said "let me think about it," and you never heard from them again.

How to use it today:

Step What to do Time
1 Fill in the five blanks in the Fill-Ins box below once. Every template uses them. 3 min
2 Read The Texting Rules (10 min, once). Then paste Missed-Call Text #1 into your phone's auto-reply, your answering app or your field-service software's missed-call text-back setting. 5 min
3 Put the Quote Follow-Up Sequence on your calendar or in your software as reminders: Day 1, 3, 7, 14, 21. 5 min
4 Print the Follow-Up Tracker page and stick it by the desk, or use the spreadsheet. 2 min

Fill-Ins. Replace these everywhere: {Business} your company name · {You} your first name · {Phone} your callback number · {Link} your booking link or website (optional) · {Trade} what you do (e.g. "AC repair", "house cleaning")

{First} is the customer's first name. {Job} is the job you quoted. {Price} is the quoted price.

A note on tone. Every message here is written to sound like a busy, honest tradesperson, not a marketing department. Keep them short. Texts that look like ads get ignored. Texts that look like a person get answered.

Part 1 — Missed-Call Text-Back

Send within 5 minutes of the missed call, faster if you can. Speed matters more than wording. Most field-service apps (Jobber, Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, Workiz and others) and most business phone apps (Google Voice, OpenPhone/Quo, RingCentral, Grasshopper) have an automatic missed-call text setting. If yours doesn't, set your phone's "busy" auto-reply and send by hand.

Message type → 1 · Reply (they contacted you; stay on their request, max 3 touches, no offers). See The Texting Rules.

Text #1 — Standard (business hours) ★ start with this one

Hi, this is {You} with {Business}. Sorry I missed your call, I'm on a job right now. What can I help you with? Reply here and I'll get back to you within the hour.

Text #2 — After hours

Hi, it's {You} at {Business}. We're closed for the night, but I saw your call. Reply with what you need and the best time to reach you, and I'll call first thing in the morning. If it's an emergency, reply URGENT.

Text #3 — Weekend

Thanks for calling {Business}! We're off for the weekend but checking messages. Tell me what's going on and I'll get you on the schedule. Monday mornings fill up fast, so I'll hold a spot if you reply today.

Text #4 — Emergency trades (plumbing, HVAC, electrical, restoration)

This is {Business}, sorry we missed you. If you have water leaking, no heat/AC, sparking or a gas smell, reply NOW and we'll call you right back. For gas smells, leave the house and call your gas company first. Otherwise reply with a quick description and we'll get you scheduled.

Text #5 — Booking-link version

Hi, {You} from {Business} here. Missed your call! Fastest way to get on the schedule is here: {Link}. Or just reply with what you need and I'll text you back.

Text #6 — Second touch (if no reply after 2–3 hours)

Just checking you got sorted, {First}. Still happy to help with that if you need it. I have an opening {tomorrow morning / Thursday afternoon}.

Why the second touch works: people call three companies at once. The first one to actually talk to them usually wins. The specific opening makes it easy to say yes.

Text #7 — Final touch (next day, no reply)

No worries if you found someone, {First}! If you still need {Trade}, we're here. Just reply to this text. — {You}, {Business}

That's the last one. Three touches, then stop. More than that starts to feel pushy, and the conversation is over unless they reply.

Voicemail greeting (record this — 20 seconds)

"You've reached {Business}, this is {You}. I'm probably on a job. You'll get a text from this number in the next few minutes. Just reply to it with what you need, it's the fastest way to reach me. If it's an emergency, say 'emergency' in your message and I'll call right back."

This tells callers to expect the text, so they don't ignore it as spam.

When they reply: the 3-question qualifier

Keep it to three questions so it doesn't feel like a form: 1. "What's going on?" (the problem) 2. "What's the address or zip?" (are they in your area) 3. "When works best for you, mornings or afternoons?" (move to booking)

Then: "Perfect. I can do {day} between {time window}. Want me to lock that in?"

Part 2 — The Quote Follow-Up Sequence

Most quotes aren't lost to a cheaper competitor. They're lost to silence. The homeowner got busy, forgot, or felt awkward asking a question. This 5-touch sequence over 21 days is polite, useful and easy to run.

Message type → 2 · Service (ask "Okay if I text you to follow up on this quote?" when you give it, and note the answer. If they say no, use email for the follow-ups.)

Rules that make it work - Every touch gives them something: an answer, an option, a reason. Never just "checking in." - Mix text and email. Some people live in one, not the other. - Stop the moment they say yes, no, or "not now." - "No" is a fine answer. Ask why (Touch 5) and you'll learn how to price better.

Touch 1 — Day 0/1 · Text · "Here's your quote"

Hi {First}, it's {You} from {Business}. Your quote for {Job} is in your email. Any questions at all, just reply here. Happy to walk you through it.

Touch 2 — Day 3 · Email · "The question most people ask"

Subject: Your {Job} quote, plus the question most people ask

Hi {First},

Following up on the {Job} quote I sent over on {date}.

The question I get most often is "why does it cost this much?" Here's the honest breakdown: {one or two sentences, e.g. "about half is the unit itself, the rest is the labor to install it to code and haul the old one away"}.

If anything in the quote is unclear, or you want to see a lower-cost option, just reply and I'll put one together.

Thanks, {You} {Business} · {Phone}

Touch 3 — Day 7 · Text · "Options"

Hi {First}, {You} again. If the {Job} quote is more than you planned, I can do a {smaller scope / phased / basic} version for around {lower price}. Want me to send that over?

Why it works: when price is the silent objection, giving them a smaller option lets them reply without admitting it.

Touch 4 — Day 14 · Email · "Schedule / timing"

Subject: Holding a spot for {Job}?

Hi {First},

Quick one. Our schedule for {month} is starting to fill. If you'd like the {Job} done before {season/holiday/the hot weather}, I can hold {date option 1} or {date option 2} for you.

If the timing isn't right, no problem at all. Just let me know and I'll stop nudging.

{You}

Only say the schedule is filling if it's true. Honesty keeps your reputation.

Touch 5 — Day 21 · Text · "Closing the loop"

Hi {First}, I'll close out your {Job} quote this week so I'm not bugging you. If you went another way, totally fine. Would you mind telling me why? One word is plenty (price / timing / went with someone else). It helps me a lot. Thanks either way! — {You}

This "break-up" message often gets the most replies of the whole sequence, and a surprising number are "Actually, can we still do it?"

Big-ticket version (quotes over ~$3,000)

Big jobs take longer to decide on. Add these two touches and stretch the schedule to 30 days: - Day 10 · Email — "Financing / payment options": "Some customers prefer to spread the cost. We offer {financing partner / 2–3 payments}. Here's how it works: …" - Day 30 · Phone call: a real call. "Hi {First}, it's {You} from {Business}. Calling about the {Job} quote. No pressure, I just wanted to see whether you had any questions I could answer."

If they reply "too expensive"

Totally fair, thanks for being straight with me. Can I ask what you were hoping to spend? Sometimes I can change the scope, the materials or the timing to get closer. If not, no hard feelings.

If they reply "we went with someone else"

Thanks for letting me know, {First}. I appreciate it. If anything comes up down the road, I'm a text away. Good luck with the project!

(Then add them to your rebooking list. See the Unghosted System.)

Part 3 — Trade Playbooks

The templates above work as written for any home-service business. This part tunes them to the jobs and hesitations each trade sees every week. Find your trade, and skip the rest.

HVAC & Plumbing

Missed calls: emergency versions

Message type → 1 · Reply

HVAC: no heat / no cool

Hi, {You} with {Business}. Sorry I missed you, I'm on a call. Is your system not heating or cooling right now? Reply with what's happening and your zip and I'll get back to you fast. No heat or AC with kids or seniors at home? Reply URGENT.

Plumbing: active leak

This is {You} at {Business}, sorry I missed your call! If water is leaking right now, turn off the main shutoff (usually near the water heater or where the line enters the house) and reply URGENT. Otherwise reply with what's going on and I'll get back to you shortly.

Safety first: for a gas smell, the message should always say "leave the house and call your gas company" before anything else.

The four quotes that go quiet most often

Message type → 2 · Service (follow-ups on a quote they requested; get their OK to text when you quote)

Quote Why it stalls The follow-up angle that works
AC / furnace replacement ($5k–$15k+) Sticker shock, comparing 2–3 bids, spouse decision Explain what the price includes, offer a repair-vs-replace comparison, mention financing at Day 10
Water heater replacement They're living with cold showers and decide fast, so the first reply wins Speed: same-day text, specific install times
Repipe / sewer line / slab leak Big, scary, unexpected A plain explanation of the problem, and a phased option
Repair the tech recommended but the customer postponed "We'll wait and see" A no-pressure check-in before the season it's likely to fail

Replacement quote: what's included (Day 3 email insert, Type 2 · Service)

"The price covers the equipment, the install to code, permits and inspection, haul-away of the old unit, and the {X}-year labor warranty, so there are no surprise bills later. If you'd like, I can also send a side-by-side of repairing your current system versus replacing it."

Repair vs. replace (Day 7 text, Type 2 · Service)

Hi {First}, {You} again. Some folks find it easier to decide with the numbers side by side: repairing your current {system} is about ${repair} and should buy you {estimate}; replacing is ${replace} with a {X}-year warranty. Want me to send that comparison?

Financing (Day 10 email, big tickets, Type 2 · Service)

Many customers prefer to spread the cost of a new {system}. We offer {financing partner / payment options}: {one-line terms, accurate and complete}. Want me to send the details for your quote?

Financing details must be accurate and complete. Only mention terms you actually offer, and follow your lender's advertising rules.

Water heater: speed reply (Type 2 · Service)

Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. I can install your new water heater {today after 3 / tomorrow morning}. Want me to lock in one of those times?

Sewer / repipe: plain-English explainer (Type 2 · Service)

Hi {First}, quick recap of what we found: {one-sentence problem in plain words}. The full fix is ${full}. If it's easier, we can do it in two phases: {phase 1} now for ${p1}, and {phase 2} later. Happy to walk you through it on the phone.

Honest replies to the objections you hear most

They say You reply
"It's still working, why tune it up?" "Totally fair. Most tune-ups are about catching a $20 part before it takes out a $1,500 one. If it checks out fine, you've got peace of mind for the season."
"Another company quoted less." "Could you check whether theirs includes the permit, haul-away and labor warranty? If it's apples to apples, I'll tell you honestly whether I can match it."
"Can't you just patch it?" "I can, and I'll quote both. The patch is ${x} and usually buys {time}; the fix is ${y} and is guaranteed. Your call."
"I need to think about it." "Of course, it's a big decision. Want me to send the repair-vs-replace numbers so you can compare them side by side?"
"That's a lot for an hour." "I get it. You're paying for the truck being stocked with the right parts, the license and the guarantee as well as the hour. If it's not fixed, you don't pay twice."

Timing that's honest and effective

  • HVAC: replacement quotes made in shoulder seasons (spring, fall) can wait; summer and winter breakdowns can't. Match urgency to the season, and never invent it.
  • Plumbing: most plumbing quotes are decided within days. Front-load your follow-up (Day 0, 1, 3), then slow down.
  • Both: "the schedule is filling" only when it truly is.

Electrical

Message type → 1 · Reply

Missed call (safety first)

This is {You} with {Business}, sorry I missed you. If you see sparks, smell burning or have a panel that's hot to the touch, turn off the main breaker if it's safe and call 911 if there's fire. Otherwise reply with what's going on and I'll get right back to you.

Message type → 2 · Service

The quote that stalls: panel upgrades, EV chargers, generators. They're big, unfamiliar purchases.

Hi {First}, quick recap of your {job} quote: the price includes the permit and inspection, so the work is on record for your insurance and when you sell. Want me to walk you through it on a 5-minute call?

Objection: "My brother-in-law can do it." → "Totally understand. Just know unpermitted work can cause trouble with insurance claims and home sales. If you go that way, I'm happy to inspect it after."

House Cleaning

Message type → 1 · Reply

Missed call

Hi! This is {You} from {Business}. Sorry I missed your call. I'm with a client right now. Are you looking for a one-time clean or regular service? Reply with your zip and roughly how many bedrooms and bathrooms, and I'll send you a quote today.

Message type → 2 · Service

The quote that stalls: first-time deep cleans. They're worried about price and about strangers in the house.

Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. Your quote includes all supplies, the same team each visit, and our re-clean guarantee: if anything's missed, we come back within 24 hours. Happy to answer any questions, or you're welcome to be home for the first clean.

Objection: "Another service is cheaper." → "They might be! Worth asking whether they bring supplies, are insured, and come back if something's missed. If they do, great. If not, that's what the difference covers."

Lawn Care & Landscaping

Message type → 1 · Reply

Missed call

Hi, this is {You} with {Business}, sorry I missed your call. I'm probably behind a mower! Reply with your address or zip and what you need (mowing, cleanup, landscaping) and I'll send you a quote.

Message type → 2 · Service

The quote that stalls: full-season agreements and landscaping projects.

Hi {First}, {You} again. To compare quotes easily: ours is the full-season price, with weekly visits, edging and cleanup every time, and we skip (and don't charge for) weeks when the grass isn't growing. Any questions, just reply.

Objection: "The kid down the street does it for $30." → "He might do a great job! What you get with us is insurance, reliable weekly timing and cleanup every visit. If that matters, we're a good fit."

Pest Control

Message type → 1 · Reply

Missed call

Hi, {You} from {Business}. Sorry I missed your call! What are you seeing (ants, rodents, termites, bed bugs, something else)? Reply with a quick description and your zip and I'll get back to you today.

Message type → 2 · Service

The quote that stalls: quarterly plans after a one-time treatment.

Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. Your quote is for a full treatment with a follow-up visit included. If they come back between treatments, so do we, at no charge. Want me to get you scheduled?

Objection: "I'll buy spray at the hardware store." → "That can work for a few ants! Store sprays usually kill what you see but don't reach the colony, so they come back. If yours do, give me a text."

Every other trade

Roofing, garage doors, pools, windows, gutters, handyman and others: use the general templates in Parts 1 and 2, and borrow the play closest to your work. Big-ticket jobs follow the HVAC replacement play; same-day jobs follow the water heater play; recurring services follow the cleaning or pest play.

Part 4 — Phone Scripts

Calling back a missed caller

"Hi, is this {First}? This is {You} from {Business}. You called us a little while ago and I'm sorry I missed you. I was on a job. What's going on?"

Then use the 3-question qualifier from Part 1.

Quote follow-up call (Day 30 or big tickets)

"Hi {First}, it's {You} from {Business}. I'm calling about the {Job} quote. I'm not calling to pressure you, I just know quotes can be confusing. Was there anything in it you'd like me to explain?"

(Listen. Don't fill silence.)

If interested: "Great, the earliest I can get you in is {date}. Does that work?" If not now: "No problem. Would it help if I checked back in {a month / spring}?" If no: "Totally understand. Do you mind if I ask what made the decision? It helps me improve."

Part 5 — Texting the Right Way

Every template in this kit is labeled with a message type. The full rules are in the included guide, The Texting Rules. Read it once before you turn anything on. The short version:

Template Type Permission you need
Missed-call texts #1–#7 1 · Reply They called you. Stay on topic, max 3 touches
Quote follow-up, touches 1–5 (within ~3 weeks) 2 · Service Their OK to text about the quote. Ask when you quote, note it
Reviving a quote months later 3 · Marketing Written consent first, or use email
Phone scripts Live calls A real person dialing by hand. Respect quiet hours and do-not-call requests

Three rules that cover most situations: 1. No offers inside Type 1 or Type 2 messages. 2. Texts only between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. in the customer's time zone (except an immediate reply to an emergency). 3. Any request to stop means stop, right away, everywhere.
